automation_evidence.quote: Traffic-R1 reduced the average and maximum queue lengths by 9.3% and 4.4%, respectively. Furthermore, it achieved a substantial 75% reduction in the human labor required for daily operations.

metric_evidence.quote: As shown in Table 2, our model significantly outperforms all baselines, demonstrating strong generalization for real-world deployment.

evidence.quote: Stable OOD generalization. Traffic-R1 maintains consistent performance across diverse OOD scenarios and outperforms larger general LLMs and LLMLight by over 30% across metrics

practical_problems.note: Table 3 evaluates local and network-wide out-of-distribution incidents; the ablation (Figure 6) also covers OOD tasks.

evidence.quote: We conducted a six-week in-situ evaluation to quantify the performance of Traffic-R1. The experiment was structured as an A/B test, comparing our proposed system against the baseline

practical_problems.note: Six-week A/B test against manual control at 10 intersections; 3B model sized for edge inference.

evidence.quote: We achieve human-like reasoning for explainable TSC through self-iteration of the reinforced LLM.

practical_problems.note: Explainable reasoning is claimed but no faithfulness or operator-review study is reported.

summary: A 3B LLM trained by offline and online RL controls traffic signals; it beats baselines on public and out-of-distribution incident tasks and a six-week A/B test shows 9.3% shorter average queues than manual control and 75% less operator labor.
